recorded_items.candidate_name: Starwood Real Estate Income Trust × Apollo affordable-housing JV recapitalization

payload.reported_structure: Starwood Real Estate Income Trust formed a Delaware LLC joint venture holding approximately 120 U.S. affordable-housing properties. Apollo funds and affiliates made a source-native $1.02 billion high-grade investment for Class B units representing 41.5% of the JV; Starwood retained 58.5%, full asset-management responsibility and operational control.
payload.accounting_treatment: Starwood stated that it would consolidate the JV and classify Apollo's interest as a redeemable noncontrolling interest, with no gain or loss recognized on formation.

payload.reported_structure: Available portfolio cash is distributed in part to Apollo, while Starwood guarantees Apollo distributions sufficient to produce an annual minimum yield on the investment; the minimum yield increases over time. Starwood has a call option to redeem Apollo's interest, and if exercised between the fifth and tenth anniversaries the call price is calculated to provide Apollo a capped 7% IRR.
unknowns: terms outside the fifth-to-tenth-anniversary call window

payload.inference: The transaction functions as a portfolio-level recapitalization: Starwood monetizes a minority economic interest in an existing asset pool without surrendering operating control, then uses the external capital to repay credit facilities. Apollo receives an equity interest combined with contractual downside/return protection through a guaranteed minimum yield and a future repurchase formula, while Starwood preserves majority ownership and operational control.
payload.mechanism: A controlled asset pool is placed in a JV; an external capital provider buys a minority class; proceeds move back to the sponsor for balance-sheet repair; the sponsor keeps management/control; contractual distributions and a repurchase option shape the investor's return profile.
payload.limitations: DISCOVERY did not establish the actual minimum yield, full waterfall, portfolio valuation, leverage reduction, realized interest savings, or whether the structure outperforms an outright asset sale or conventional refinancing.
